overview: The Ministry of Steel provides financial assistance through the Government funded scheme 'Promotion of Research and Development in the steel sector' to pursue R&D addressing technological issues faced by the sector and for indigenous development of processes/technologies. The thrust areas include development of new alternate processes & technologies to address challenges such as climate change (green steel production, H2 based steel production, CCUS etc.), waste utilization, and resource efficiency. The scheme supports R&D work at lab scale, bench scale, and scale-up to pilot/demonstration plants, with financial assistance varying by applicant type: up to 50% for industrial/commercial organisations, up to 70% for academic institutions and national/regional research laboratories, and up to 40% for pilot/demonstration scale projects with the balance met by industrial partners. Joint proposals with other laboratories/institutions/industry are encouraged, and individual innovators and start-ups in the steel sector are granted access to scheme-funded facilities and equipment.
objectives: To catalyze innovation, sustainability, and global competitiveness in the steel sector by funding cutting-edge research and development initiatives.
To empower industry, academia, start-ups, and individual innovators to collaboratively address technological challenges.
To enhance resource efficiency and accelerate the adoption of advanced materials and processes for a resilient and future-ready steel ecosystem.
To promote Research & Development in the Iron & Steel Sector by providing financial support to stakeholders to address R&D needs of national importance.
To develop innovative/path breaking technologies for utilization of iron ore fines and non-coking coal.
To beneficiate raw materials like iron ore, coal etc. and agglomeration.
To improve quality of steel produced through various routes of steel making including the Induction Furnace route.
To develop commercially viable technology for utilization of steel plant and mine wastes including LD/EAF/IF Slag.
To develop indigenous technologies for improved processes and product development aimed at reducing import dependency.
To pursue R&D on steel intensive design of building/bridges/structures to increase usage/consumption of steel.
To develop innovative solutions for addressing challenges faced by the iron & steel industry.
To pursue R&D on any other subject of national importance concerning the Iron & Steel sector.
eligibility: R&D Project Proposals are invited from stakeholders viz. reputed Academic Institutions, Research Laboratories and Indian Steel Companies for pursuing R&D projects for the benefit of the Iron & Steel Sector in the country. The scheme was introduced in the year 2009-10, based on the recommendation of the Working Group for Iron & Steel Industry for the 11th Five Year Plan. Subsequently, the scheme has been continued further and the current approval is till March 2031. The Scheme is of continuous nature since the R&D projects being pursued under the scheme are of varying durations, usually 2-3 years duration and new projects are being approved every year. Further, R&D has very long gestation periods before any fruitful results can be achieved. Accordingly, the scheme needs to be continued further to provide uninterrupted support to the stakeholders on in carrying our R&D for the Iron & Steel sector.
benefits: Financial support for R&D projects, access to scheme-funded facilities and equipment (e.g., at NML and IIMT) for individual innovators and start-ups, provision for joint proposals with other laboratories/institutions/industry, and support for R&D work at lab scale, bench scale, and scale-up to pilot/demonstration plants. The scheme also encourages commercialization and technology development, with a heavy bias towards projects amenable to commercialization, technology development and immediate absorption by the industry.
financial_support: The budget allocated for the scheme is around Rs 5-10 Crore per year. Financial assistance is provided as follows: for Industrial/Commercial organisations pursuing R&D projects with Plan Fund, financial assistance of upto 50% of the total cost is permissible; for Academic Institutions & National/Regional Research Laboratories, financial assistance of upto 70% is permissible (preference given to R&D project having tie-up with user industry); for Pilot/Demonstration Scale R&D projects, financial contribution from Plan Fund will be limited to upto 40% & the balance to be met by the industrial partner; Financial assistance up to 100% for multidimensional team shall be under discretion of Secretary Steel on merit of the proposal. The Ministry shall create a categorized Pool of industrial partners, including MSMEs, aligned with key thrust areas. If a Principal Investigator (PI) cannot secure industry partnership, the Ministry will route the proposal to the relevant pool for review and potential funding/collaboration.
application_process: 1. Applicants are requested to go through guidelines, formats and terms & conditions given as Annexures before submitting the R&D Proposals. 2. R&D Proposals duly signed and forwarded by Head of the Institutions/Organisations/Companies should be uploaded to the Ministry of Steel R & D portal (https://research.steel.gov.in/Applicant) as well as sent in Pdf to mosteel-rd@gov.in. 3. For further queries, contact Technical Division, Ministry of Steel at Tel: 011-26773364. 4. Submission of R&D proposals is continuous and there is no last date for submission of the proposals (open ended).
required_documents: R&D proposals duly signed and forwarded by Head of the Institutions/Organisations/Companies
Pdf copy of the proposal to be sent to mosteel-rd@gov.in
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
contact_details: Technical Division, Ministry of Steel, Tel: 011-26773364, e-mail: mosteel-rd@gov.in
caveats: Basic research should not be funded or should be funded in much less quantum & numbers through this scheme as there are other agencies of the Government to promote basic research like Dept. of Science & Technology.

Researchers may be asked to submit their proposal jointly in collaboration with one or more industry partners in which the industry partner is willing to fund at least 15% of the research expenditure and in return may claim the right of first use of the research outcomes.

The R&D Implementing Agency must submit beforehand the road map for commercialisation that they will take up on successful completion of the R&D project and indicate the stakeholders to be associated by them for the commercialisation activities.

The Grantee institution may use the IPR arising out of the Ministry funded project while the patent may be filed in the name(s) of inventor(s)/ the institution(s). In cases of collaborative projects, the IP rights would be appropriately shared among the collaborators.
For Intellectual Property proposed for commercial usage, the provisions of licensing may be mutually agreed upon with the grantee institution(s) possessing the IPR.

The Ministry shall be duly informed by the grantee institution about the patents filed/granted and IPR emerging out of the R&D project on yearly basis during the project tenure and following 5 years period after completion of the project.

In case of any commercial event like trading/ selling/ transferring /licensing of IP rights, the grantee institution shall provide information to the Ministry within a period of 6 weeks from the closure of the agreement.
While licensing of patents/transfer or commercialization of technology, the grantee institution shall ensure that the interests of India and its citizens are fully protected.
The institution is permitted to retain the benefits and earnings arising out of the IPR for plough back to conduct research/research related activities.
Notwithstanding the above, the Ministry reserves the right to take over ownership of the rights of IP in case of national priority without any compensation to the grantee institution.

The research organization should supply along with a research proposal a skill development plan through which M.Tech./B.Tech./ Ph.D. students in the field of metallurgy will be trained in sophisticated equipments through formal means like skill development workshop, training apprenticeships etc.

A dissemination plan to be in place at the time of research proposal, whereby the researcher will conduct seminars not just for the research community, but also for academic community, especially for students in junior levels.

Stricter monitoring through a LOGFRAME approach: Logframes are a tool for monitoring and evaluation that originated from a planning approach used by the US military. It has since then become a standard tool for monitoring of internationally granted projects. In its simplest form a logframe is a 4x4 matrix with 16 cells. In it, you note down what you want to achieve while granting a project and how you’ll get there and in what time frame. This brings clarity to fund projects and also makes monitoring very objective. The Logframe matrix to be submitted by the researcher as part of the R&D proposal submitted for consideration.
Declarations in writing be obtained from the R&D agencies that similar projects have not be pursued earlier by them or other organizations.
In case substantial unspent grants are lying with an organisation, grants in new projects should not be released. Use of unutilised funds from existing projects in new projects may be insisted upon.
There should be a cap on the funding on overheads. It can be around 10-15% of the total project cost subject to a cap of 25 lakhs.

Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided from Government for R&D projects pursued by Research Laboratories, Academic Institutions & Steel Companies, in line with the objectives of the scheme. Projects with Industrial Partnership (joint collaborative projects) will be preferred. For commercial organisations Government assistance will be upto 50% of the cost of the project.

An Evaluation Group comprising members from Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, DRDO, DSIR, DST, Premiere Academic Institutions and Industry, carry out evaluation of the R&D proposals received for funding under the scheme.

A Project Approval and Monitoring Committee (PAMC) under the Chairmanship of Additional Secretary & Financial Adviser and Joint Secretary, Ministry of Steel, Director IIT Kharagpur, Director IMMT, Director NML, Representative from MSME are the 2nd Stage approving body for the R&D proposals recommended by Evaluation Group.
Final approval is accorded by the designated authority based on the cost of the project as per the guidelines issued by Department of Expenditure.

The R&D Agency must ensure that no grant in aid for the same purpose has been availed from any other Ministry/Department of the Government of India or State Government. Undertaking shall be sought from the R&D Agency.
Declaration in writing be obtained from the implementing agencies that the terms & conditions of the sanction are acceptable to them.
